## Mechanism research and data audit

Literature and source-schema work are in LITERATURE.md and DATA_ACCESS_AUDIT.md. Primary evidence supports a specific prior-close inventory-risk explanation for an overnight drift; it does not establish profitable US cash-open failed-auction reversal. The original authors report the European-opening drift weakened after2021. A positive overnight price return is not a measured dealer inventory position.

Current OHLCV/trade-count data do not have genuine aggressor side, bid/ask or contract mapping. Official source fixtures contain only four ESH1 trades spanning under half a second. They support parser verification only. Four tests verify source B/A signing, unknown-side preservation, passive-event exclusion and rejection of candle-only data. No source signing was invented.

**Full overnight-inventory + failed-auction + signed-flow hypothesis: DATA-BLOCKED, not scientifically rejected.** A suitable authorized contract-level trade/quote export covering many sessions and regimes is the missing prerequisite. No purchase or restricted access is authorized or attempted.

## Completed successive experiments

S001 preregistered an opening failure of the overnight range, known at09:45, and tested the availability bound—not trading returns. On194eligible full sessions, one-sided events occurred43times inMES(22.2%) and53times inMNQ(27.3%). Even a generous any-failure bound is22.7%/27.3%. Gap-proxy conditioning reduced coverage further. A system tradingonlythoseevents cannot achieve$100on70%ofALLeligible days even with perfect conditional predictions. This closes its standalone income-target architecture; it does not reject a possible fleet sleeve or signed-flow predictive contribution.

S003 tested one fixed2–3a.m.NewYork markout on201eligible2026weekdays, using one micro, fixed fees and stressed market friction. It partially investigates the published mechanism; it cannot replicate pre2021regime decay or actual inventory conditioning. MES was negative. S004 is closed without tuning its stop/hour. The protective constraint removed the attractive fixed-hold result. That teaches that the apparent drift cannot be converted to the required account-safe outcome by this simple variant; it does not prove all overnight mechanisms impossible.
